newsitem.title: UK: Severn Trent spurts up on renewed bid talk.
newsitem.headline: Severn Trent spurts up on renewed bid talk.

text.p: Shares in Severn Trent Plc gushed 17-1/2p to a 1997 high of 766p on Friday amid rumours that a predator could have its eye on the water and sewage company, dealers and market makers said.
"It's an old chestnut but there is talk that someone might be thinking of making a bid," one market maker said.
Water sector analysts were sceptical about the likelihood of a bid for Severn Trent following a flood of takeovers in the utilities sector over the past few years.
"A bid for Severn Trent seems very unlikely, especially ahead of the (British) election," one analyst who wished to remain anonymous said.
"If there is a change of regime it would be much more difficult to buy a water company under a Labour government than a Tory(Conservative) government."
The opposition Labour Party, which currently leads the ruling Conservatives by around 20 percentage points in opinion polls, is odds on favourite to win the May 1 election.
Labour, which lobbied against the privatisation of nationalised utility companies, is committed to levying a "windfall tax" on the utilities should it come into power.
The bid speculation added sparkle to the water sector, dealers said. United Utilities Plc swelled 13p to 671-1/2, Thames Water Plc rose 12-1/2p to 689p, and Wessex Water Plc added 11-1/2p to 386-1/2.
